name: What Semantics Studies — semantics fundamentals record
title: What Semantics Studies — Fundamentals of Semantics
description: Signature edition. This entry teaches What Semantics Studies as part of the fundamentals of semantics, presented the Signature way: from first principles, in plain language, building toward mastery. It sits at the Foundations tier of the teaching ladder, where each idea earns its place before the next is introduced. Signature-authored and Signature-labeled throughout.
overview: In the Signature teaching of semantics, What Semantics Studies is a load-bearing idea: understand it and much of the field clicks into place. Lexical meaning means what words mean, from prototypes to features. Reference means how words hook onto the world. Together these ideas give the learner working intuition, not just vocabulary. The Signature presentation stresses why each principle holds, shows where it is used in real practice, and connects it forward to the Foundations material that follows.
core_concepts: Lexical meaning: what words mean, from prototypes to features.
Reference: how words hook onto the world.
key_laws: Compositionality: the meaning of the whole determined by parts and syntax.
vocabulary: Denotation: the things a word refers to; connotation its associations.
Deixis: meaning depending on context like I, here, now.
methods: Truth-conditional analysis: testing meanings against scenarios.
history: Semantics grew from 19th-century philology; Frege's logic and Tarski's truth founded formal approaches. Grice's pragmatics and cognitive linguistics added use and mind, making meaning study richly interdisciplinary.
key_points: Lexical meaning: what words mean, from prototypes to features.
Reference: how words hook onto the world.
Key vocabulary: Denotation — the things a word refers to; connotation its associations.; Deixis — meaning depending on context like I, here, now..
Governing principle: Compositionality: the meaning of the whole determined by parts and syntax.
how_it_works: The Signature learner approaches What Semantics Studies by anchoring it to what is already known: Denotation (the things a word refers to; connotation its associations.), then Deixis (meaning depending on context like I, here, now.). The working method is Truth-conditional analysis: testing meanings against scenarios. Practice means rehearsing the idea until it can be reconstructed from scratch, which is exactly what the accompanying study program drills.

name: The Future of Semantics — semantics fundamentals record
title: The Future of Semantics — Fundamentals of Semantics
description: Signature edition. This entry teaches The Future of Semantics as part of the fundamentals of semantics, presented the Signature way: from first principles, in plain language, building toward mastery. It sits at the Advanced tier of the teaching ladder, where each idea earns its place before the next is introduced. Signature-authored and Signature-labeled throughout.
overview: In the Signature teaching of semantics, The Future of Semantics is a load-bearing idea: understand it and much of the field clicks into place. Reference means how words hook onto the world. Formal semantics means logic-based models of meaning composition. Together these ideas give the learner working intuition, not just vocabulary. The Signature presentation stresses why each principle holds, shows where it is used in real practice, and connects it forward to the Advanced material that follows.
core_concepts: Reference: how words hook onto the world.
Formal semantics: logic-based models of meaning composition.
key_laws: Grice's maxims: the cooperative principles generating implicatures.
Verification: meaning connected to truth conditions.
vocabulary: Entailment: one sentence guaranteeing another's truth.
Speech act: what utterances do, promising, ordering, asserting.
methods: Paraphrase tests: revealing meaning differences.
history: Semantics grew from 19th-century philology; Frege's logic and Tarski's truth founded formal approaches. Grice's pragmatics and cognitive linguistics added use and mind, making meaning study richly interdisciplinary.
key_points: Reference: how words hook onto the world.
Formal semantics: logic-based models of meaning composition.
Key vocabulary: Entailment — one sentence guaranteeing another's truth.; Speech act — what utterances do, promising, ordering, asserting..
Governing principle: Grice's maxims: the cooperative principles generating implicatures.
how_it_works: The Signature learner approaches The Future of Semantics by anchoring it to what is already known: Entailment (one sentence guaranteeing another's truth.), then Speech act (what utterances do, promising, ordering, asserting.). The working method is Paraphrase tests: revealing meaning differences. Practice means rehearsing the idea until it can be reconstructed from scratch, which is exactly what the accompanying study program drills.
